gen-gf-yomogi-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain sans stripe of constant ink, its curves opening generously, which makes it dependable. Yomogi's hand-drawn crescent c's loosen the mood above it.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akari-fs-neco: Neco swells in measured steps from hairline to stem, its letters never pinching shut, and gives the page a dignified footing. Yuji Hentaigana Akari looks best a touch larger.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akari-fs-rowan: Big side gaps give Yuji Hentaigana Akari its relaxed, hand-drawn look. It earns its keep large and brief, while Rowan's gently thinning bowls and generous curves carry the rest.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akari-fs-synonym: Synonym reads like a plain sans stripe of constant ink, with generous openings in every curve and nothing fussy. Yuji Hentaigana Akari adds a relaxed, personal hand, and its low weight change sits oddly well against that stencil-flat line.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akebono-fs-neco: Friendly and inviting, Yuji Hentaigana Akebono looks like casual pen-and-paper writing, with light strokes that recede only slightly. It earns its keep big and brief, while Neco keeps things dignified.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akebono-fs-synony: Loose, inked and approachable, Yuji Hentaigana Akebono leaves considerable room between its letters. And Synonym answers it with a single-weight line, like a plotter pen, and generous curves.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akebono-plus-jaka: Inviting is the first word for Yuji Hentaigana Akebono, with casual pen-and-paper letters whose apertures stay open even tiny. Plus Jakarta Sans brings modern precision, its monoline stems matching the hairlines because there are none.
gen-gf-yuji-hentaigana-akebono-space-gro: Yuji Hentaigana Akebono is the loose, friendly voice. Its pen-and-paper letters do best up top, while Space Grotesk does its best work below, with geometric counters and constant-width ribbons forming each glyph.
gen-gf-zen-loop-fs-rowan: Zen Loop keeps its stroke widths steady and its c forms open. Rowan sits below it with generous curves and thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones, a literary, friendly counterweight.
gen-gloria-hallelujah-fs-amulya: Gloria Hallelujah has comic energy, with tubular strokes like bent copper pipe and wide, easy turns in its s shapes. And Amulya stays modern and contemporary, keeping the gaps in its curves generous.
